title: Projective logarithmic resolution over an excellent affine base
statement: Let $A$ be an excellent Noetherian ring [def-exc-excellent-ring], put $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $(V,M)$ be an integral fs log regular scheme, quasi-projective of finite type over $B$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-projective over a scheme $B$ means admitting a locally closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$; projective means a closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$ followed by projection [def-kun-projective]. There exists a finite tower of saturated log blowups $b:(Y,M_Y)\to(V,M)$ whose underlying composite is projective and birational, with $Y$ integral and regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The log morphism $b$ is log etale [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. For any locally Noetherian fs log scheme $D$ and any log-smooth morphism $(V,M)\to D$, the composite $(Y,M_Y)\to D$ is log smooth. Birational means inducing an isomorphism between dense opens; length-zero towers are allowed.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.4.6(i), 3.4.8--Theorem 3.4.9, pp.111--112; VI 1.7--1.8, p.70; XVI 3.7, p.254. Finite normalized blowup towers are projective here; the quasi-projective affine-base hypothesis gives the finite-projective-space convention.

proof.text: The base $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] therefore makes $V$ Noetherian, in particular quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. For a geometric point $\bar v$, [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart] says that $P=\overline M_{\bar v}$ is saturated and sharp. If $nh=0$ in $P^{\rm gp}$ with $n>0$, saturation applied to both $h$ and $-h$ puts both in $P$. Hence $h$ is a unit of $P$, so sharpness gives $h=0$. Thus every characteristic group is torsion free. Apply [lem-trf-monoidal-resolution-tower] to obtain a finite tower $(X_n,M_n)\to\cdots\to(X_0,M_0)=(V,M)$ along nonempty coherent log ideals $\mathcal I_i$, with all final characteristic monoids free. Denote its maps by $b_i:X_{i+1}\to X_i$.

Let $U\subset V$ be the triviality locus of $M$. By [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure], $U$ is open dense. We induct on $i$ with claim: $X_i$ is integral, quasi-projective of finite type over $B$, $(X_i,M_i)$ is log regular, and its triviality locus $U_i$ is the inverse image of $U$ and maps isomorphically to $U$. The claim for $i=0$ is the hypothesis. Suppose it holds for $i$. The finite-type-over-Noetherian result [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] ensures local Noetherianity. Apply [lem-trf-log-blowup-normalization] to $(X_i,M_i)$ and $\mathcal I_i$. It supplies a nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $J_i=\alpha(\mathcal I_i)\mathcal O_{X_i}$, identifies $X_{i+1}$ with $(\operatorname{Bl}_{J_i}X_i)^\nu$, and gives log regularity and $U_{i+1}=b_i^{-1}U_i\cong U_i$. Apply [lem-per-excellent-quasiprojective-normalized-blowup] over the original excellent affine base $B$: its hypotheses are the induction claim and the properties of $J_i$ just obtained. Its conclusions give integrality, quasi-projectivity and finite type of $X_{i+1}$, and global projectivity of $b_i$. This completes the induction, including projectivity of every map in the tower.

source.place: VIII 3.4.6(i), 3.4.8, pp.111--112, with ordinary projectivity and finite normalization hypotheses made explicit.

proof.text: Set $(Y,M_Y)=(X_n,M_n)$ and let $b:Y\to V$ be the composite. Step 2 gives integrality and log regularity of $Y$. Its characteristic monoids are free by Step 1, so [lem-trf-free-characteristic-regular-boundary] gives regularity of $Y$ and density of its triviality locus $U_n$. The induction identifies $U_n$ with $U$ under $b$, so $b$ is birational in the required dense-open sense. Repeated application of [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] to the projective maps $b_i$ makes $b$ projective in the finite-projective-space convention. If $n=0$, use the identity map: its closed immersion into $\mathbf P^0_V=V$ directly gives projectivity, and its restriction to $U$ is the identity.

For each $i$, use [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction] on $(X_i,M_i)$ and $\mathcal I_i$. On a strict etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}C$ with fs chart $P$ and finite ideal generators $E$, the saturated blowup has charts $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e^{\rm sat}])$, where $Q_e=\langle P,h-e\ (h\in E)\rangle\subset P^{\rm gp}$. The cited statement says $(Q_e^{\rm sat})^{\rm gp}=P^{\rm gp}$. Hence the compatible chart map $P\to Q_e^{\rm sat}$ has zero group kernel and cokernel. Its comparison scheme map to $\operatorname{Spec}C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q_e^{\rm sat}]$ is the identity, by the displayed tensor-product description. Thus the log etale criterion of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] applies: both orders are $1$, invertible in every ring, and the comparison is an isomorphism, hence etale. The charts cover the blowup, so each $b_i$ is log etale. This is the direct chart argument of VIII 3.3.11.

Each $b_i$ is log etale by Step 4; this is also the saturated-log-blowup clause of [lem-per-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change]. All schemes are locally Noetherian fs log schemes by Step 2, so that node applies. Its last clause says that finite saturated log blowup towers are log etale. Hence the tower $b:(Y,M_Y)\to(V,M)$ is log etale; for $n=0$ the tower has length zero and $b$ is the identity. Finally fix any locally Noetherian fs log scheme $D$ and log-smooth $g:(V,M)\to D$. The same node says that a log etale morphism followed by a log smooth morphism is log smooth. Applied to $b$ and $g$, it makes $g\circ b:(Y,M_Y)\to D$ log smooth. The tower was chosen independently of $D$ and $g$, so this proves the universally quantified last clause with the same $Y$ and $b$.
